title: Find upright rhythm and understand the running corridor
stage_label: Separate instructional session · individually authored · written athletic design reviewed
status_note: Independent programming review passed for the complete written athletic lesson. Numeric results and input fingerprints are recorded separately in the companion check/review files. Current canonical release, actual facility/readiness and the precise separate tumbling prescription remain unverified; plans are not completed athlete results.
brief: Teach comfortable upright running rhythm and recognition of build, finish, runoff and return boundaries. Count one complete selected-corridor walk before subsequent eligible easy runs. Keep five familiar strength roles equally visible without a new loading emphasis.
quality_target: The athlete recognizes the selected running finish and protected runoff, remains inside the corridor, uses its outside return and waits for release. An eligible run builds smoothly and retains comfortable rhythm through its upright segment before gradual slowing. Record the actual route and first fault; walking/marching/short starts do not establish an upright-running result.
continuity: Actual OR-01 corridor/participation or direct equivalent →OR-04 counted route walk and eligible easy rhythm task →OR-08 may change gradual intent alone at the retained route →OR-12 retains route/output while teaching rest and return responsibility. OR-02/03 actual strength, braking, stance and sport exposure inform readiness; these are offered links, not required attendance.
audience: Model cohort:15 athletes, three lanes and two qualified athletic coaches. Ages12–14 are the reference; all three age bands have explicit doses and the same ability-based gates. New participants learn route conduct in the counted E0 walk; experienced athletes retain actual capacities and can use an exact qualified main-entry choice rather than automatically repeating unneeded instruction. Five offered days are not five mandatory visits.
readiness: Review actual recent starts, running, braking, jumping, lower-body strength, sport and planned tumbling. Following OR-03 or another demanding exposure, reduced coordination/recovery selects walking rhythm and compatible L strength; attendance alone does not impose or remove running. Comfortable easy-jog ability and controlled gradual slowing must be independently known before the long easy-run branch. Neither E0 walking nor short P2 practice proves all running prerequisites. Symptoms/restrictions defer the affected action; a simpler route is not clearance.
equipment_space: UNVERIFIED MODEL:15 separate3m×3m preparation bays, peripheral coach access, three protected straight35m corridors with2m planning width each, and three separate one-way outside returns with no shared merge or crossing of forward queues. Long route:0–10m buildup,10–20m easy upright segment,20–35m gradual runoff. Limited-space route:0–5m target and5–15m runout; it changes the objective to short acceleration. These are declared teaching geometries, not source defaults or proven universal safe distances. P2 uses only the15m route even when E0/E1 use the35m corridor. Mark or cover the inactive finish clearly before release. Five suitable high push supports, five benches/light dumbbells and15mats are assumed; breathing requires five stable lower-leg supports. Actual dimensions, apparatus fit, traction, queue/return separation and sightlines must be verified.
coaching_flow: P1 stays in the personal bays with three observed groups of five. P2 and E0 use three familiar slow-travel athletes per wave, one per lane; two coaches divide that group1/2 from positions with useful sightlines. Unresolved participation needs individual instruction or an omitted attempt, not an unseen independent lane. E1 releases one athlete every30s in A1/B1/C1 through A5/B5/C5 order. Coach1 takes even zero-based release indices, coach2 odd indices; assignments repeat each round. Up to two45s walking observations may overlap. Each coach has60s between assigned starts, at least15s after the longest active observation. Coaches use verified full-corridor viewing positions; they do not shadow35m and sprint back. Waiting/returning athletes follow already understood routes and add no physical practice.
time_rules: Release times are earliest opportunities. Entry, active travel, gradual runoff, exit, outside return, turn/rejoin, instruction and transfers belong inside the model. These envelopes never force gait speed. Delay an unclear release and reduce uncompleted later work if necessary. All attempts, including faults and partial work, are counted physically; no replacement attempt or catch-up debt is created.
preparation_note: Use the complete reviewed instructional base below, retaining the existing basic march level and concluding hinge/squat checks. Its OR-01 profile names are not an attendance requirement. P1 repeats the same four basic in-place steps for a focused posture/rhythm observation. P2 is one short route rehearsal. The full selected-corridor walk occurs as counted E0 work in the main block, never as hidden preparation travel.

exercises.name: Find a comfortable upright rhythm
exercises.mapping: BASIC-MARCH-TEACH; quiet-standing alternative is separately mapped
exercises.set_purpose: One short set makes an upright trunk and relaxed opposite arm/leg rhythm visible before the running lesson. It deliberately repeats the useful basic preparation pattern with one focused observation; it does not add skipping or a technical height challenge.
exercises.execution: Stay in the assigned personal bay. Alternate four comfortable marching steps in place, two each side, at2s per step; settle2s. Keep one foot supported throughout and use relaxed opposite arm/leg motion. No forward travel or forced high knee is added.
exercises.cues: Comfortable steps; stand comfortably tall; opposite arm and leg; settle.
exercises.errors: Calling the in-place task exact traveling A-March, introducing flight, forcing thigh height, leaning back or adding repetitions while other groups work.
exercises.rationale: The target follows the standardized base and isolates the rhythm/posture needed downstream. A separate traveling A-March or A-Skip would add route or impact demands beyond this short task.
exercises.metadata: Method: counted stationary rhythm rehearsal. Tenets: Coordination/Body Control/Balance. Pattern: alternating no-flight support. Equipment: personal bay.

standard_D.variant: Basic alternating march in place — explicit stationary teaching adaptation
standard_D.effort_load: Bodyweight, easy2/10. Two seconds per comfortable walking-height step; four alternating steps, two each side, then settle2s. Use relaxed opposite arm/leg timing without a forced thigh-height target.
standard_D.notes: One foot remains supported; no flight or forward travel. Each left/right step is one count, not a two-step cycle. This is the same basic pattern used in the instructional preparation; it is not exact traveling A-March or sprint exposure.

exercises.competency: Comfortable ordinary walking/support exchange and stop-cue participation must be present. Missing or unsuitable marching selects the explicit quiet-standing task, not forced supported marching. All three ages retain this small dose; experienced athletes receive a concise cue rather than added height/flight.
exercises.progression: Hold count, comfortable height and no-flight pattern. Record first fault; stop for symptoms or lost balance. A cleaner rhythm is useful without higher effort or an A-Skip upgrade.
exercises.continuity: Actual instructional-base/OR-01 rhythm or equivalent →one counted basic rehearsal →selected corridor lesson →OR-08/12 retain actual preparation level and cue needs.

exercises.name: Rehearse the start and ordinary runout on a short route
exercises.mapping: ACC-STATIC low-intent contextual use, or WALK-CORRIDOR-TEACH; no-travel adaptations separately declared
exercises.set_purpose: One short counted rehearsal makes the release, finish marker and gradual runout concrete before the full corridor walk. It is preparation, not an unrecorded full-route test or a maximal acceleration set.
exercises.execution: The qualified low-intent route starts still in a comfortable bilateral standing stance, uses a smooth5m start, then slows gradually through10m protected runout and exits into its dedicated return. Unknown running readiness uses an ordinary15m corridor walk. Each route has its own active/return envelope below; no athlete walks the full35m route here. The main E0 task owns that longer physical orientation.
exercises.cues: Wait for release; smooth start; pass the finish; use the runout; walk back outside.
exercises.errors: Max effort from the first step, changing to a moving or three-point entry, stopping sharply at5m, entering the forward lane on return or adding a second rehearsal after a fault.
exercises.rationale: The short route rehearses the entry/finish behavior within the fixed preparation budget. Its identity is acceleration teaching or walking, even when the later objective uses a longer upright running corridor.
exercises.metadata: Method: single observed route rehearsal. Tenets: Coordination/Explosiveness/Body Control as eligible. Bodyweight; marked15m protected route and separate return.

exercises.competency: Running requires actual pain-free initiation, coordinated easy contacts and safe gradual runout plus understood release/return rules. OR-01 attendance alone is not evidence. Missing running evidence stays walking; no walking result passes acceleration. Symptoms or unsafe space defer travel or select a separately eligible stationary task.
exercises.progression: Retain standing start and easy intent. Count the first scheduled attempt, including faults, then wait for E0; no additional practice while queues form.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR-01 route/start observation or direct equivalent →one short rehearsal →E0 counted full or short corridor walk →E1 only with its own running/space readiness.

exercises.name: Walk the complete selected corridor
exercises.mapping: WALK-CORRIDOR-TEACH — ordinary route orientation, not a braking or speed test
exercises.set_purpose: This one physical walk teaches where the build, running finish, gradual runoff and outside return belong. It is counted in the lesson and workload before the athlete is asked to run that route.
exercises.execution: On the long route, walk0–10m build area,10–20m intended upright area and20–35m protected runoff, identify their markers in the coach’s allotted pause, then exit and walk back by the dedicated one-way return. On a short route, walk0–5m target and5–15m runout. Do not add a two-second athletic stick, turn-and-go or measured braking task. No-travel selection uses a quiet standing orientation while the coach explains the diagram; actual corridor travel remains unobserved.
exercises.cues: Name the finish; show the runoff; find the outside return; wait for the next release.
exercises.errors: Treating verbal knowledge as completed running, stopping at the running finish instead of using the remaining corridor, taking the forward lane back or leaving this walk out of total workload.
exercises.rationale: The main block has time for an actual whole-route walk; the short preparation budget does not. Walking before running teaches corridor recognition while output stays low.
exercises.metadata: Method: counted route walkthrough, full recovery. Tenets: Coordination/Body Control. Walking distance is separate from later running targets.

exercises.competency: Comfortable independent walking, simple release/stop communication and safe corridor/return are required. The first listed walk is the route observation, not an assumed completed prerequisite. If traffic understanding is incomplete, continue only an eligible walking or stationary teaching route. A long corridor that does not fit is a facility limitation, not an athlete failure.
exercises.progression: One walk only; no added walk to obtain a pass. Record actual route/marker/return mistakes. A corrected explanation does not retroactively turn an incomplete physical observation into a completed one.
exercises.continuity: OR-01 conduct or equivalent and P2 short observation →one counted selected-corridor walk →separately eligible E1 →OR-08/12 retain the actual route and address only the remaining gap.

exercises.name: Build smoothly into an easy upright rhythm
exercises.mapping: EASY-BUILD-RUN-TEACH; independently eligible short acceleration/walking/stationary alternatives
exercises.set_purpose: Each recovered easy-run set observes smooth buildup, comfortable upright rhythm and deliberate use of the finish/runoff. Standard D has two such attempts; compressed D has one. Standard L has one additional walking route observation; compressed L omits E1 after its counted E0 walk. No set seeks greater speed, longer distance or fatigue.
exercises.execution: Long D uses a still comfortable standing start, builds smoothly over0–10m from about2/10 toward3/10 effort, retains that relaxed effort through10–20m, then slows gradually through20–35m and exits before its outside return. This easy lesson has no maximal second half or timed fly. Limited space uses the separately labeled5m low-intent standing start plus10m runout. Walking and stationary routes retain their distinct prescriptions and results.
exercises.cues: Smooth build; comfortable tall rhythm; finish through the mark; slow gradually; return outside.
exercises.errors: Forcing upright posture immediately, sprinting all-out, reaching for stride length, treating the finish as a braking target, competing with another lane or recording a short start as upright-speed coverage.
exercises.rationale: Recovered running follows the actual corridor walk, with familiar strength afterward. The legacy stride-out’s maximal prescription is not imported into this low-intent lesson. Extra mechanics drills and a running finisher are omitted to preserve observation and recovery.
exercises.metadata: Method: recovered low-intent route/rhythm practice. Tenets: Speed/Explosiveness/Coordination/Body Control as actually practiced. Not maximal-velocity training.

timing_narrative:
**Exactly two targets,180s:** P1 uses40s:10s reminder of the already taught basic pattern while athletes remain in their bays, then three groups of five at10/20/30s. Each10s bout is4steps×2s+2s settle, or its explicit quiet-standing replacement. Last group finishes40s. No gathering to lanes is charged here. P2 uses140s:20s bay-to-queue gathering and route confirmation, then five three-athlete waves at20/40/60/80/100s. Running has15s active clearance+20s outside return; walking18s+20s. Last walking return ends138s, leaving2s. Same-lane releases20s apart require the active corridor and exit clear; the prior return may still be occupied only on that lane’s dedicated one-way return. Return turns/rejoin fit the20s allowance. Mixed walking/running waves can briefly place two athletes in the same dedicated return: a walker returns at18–38s and the next runner at35–55s. This3s overlap is allowed only with verified same-direction spacing, no catch-up and no shared merge; otherwise delay release and remove an uncompleted later attempt. Actual longer transfer, sightline or clearance requirements delay release and remove later uncompleted work; do not shorten the standard base or hurry the child.

**Counted corridor walk E0:** Main-relative0–120s covers instruction, long/short marker selection and lane/return explanation, without uncounted athlete trial runs. Five waves of three begin120/210/300/390/480s. A long walk uses45s outbound/orientation/exit (35s ordinary35m walking plus10s marker explanation/exit) and40s outside return including turn/rejoin. Its full85s envelope clears before the next90s same-lane release; final return ends565s. Short15m orientation uses20s active+20s return. Stationary orientation uses its own10s and no travel.565–660s is feedback, readiness and confirmed route/coach assignments. Walking is an observation of walking/route conduct, not a running test.

**E1 standard:** D rounds begin main-relative660s and1170s; L uses660s only. Fifteen individual starts use offsets0,30,…420s. A long easy run uses25s active (5s build,5s easy upright segment,12s gradual runoff,3s exit) plus40s outside return. A long walking follow-up uses45s active+40s return. Same-lane starts90s apart allow the85s worst route to return; alternating coaches have60s between assigned starts. The last second-round easy-run D return is1655s into the main block:42:35 session time. A D long-walking alternative returns at1675s:42:55, leaving2:05 for feedback/water/Strength transfer. The first-round L return finishes1165s into the block. Same-athlete D recovery after full return is445s for easy running or425s for the long-walking alternative. No L athlete takes a second round merely because it exists on the schedule.

**E1 compressed:** D uses only the660s round; compressed L has zero E1 sets after E0. The last easy-run D return is1145s into the25min main block:29:05 session time. The D long-walking alternative ends1165s into the block:29:25, leaving5:35 for feedback/water/Strength setup. Compressed L has no follow-up and does not use this later slot. Short/standing routes finish earlier without adding attempts.

**Balanced Strength:** standard gives six minutes each:45–51 knee,51–57 hip,57–63 push,63–69 pull,69–75 brace. Each block reserves90s for demonstration/apparatus and groups begin90/165/240s. Compressed gives four minutes each:35–39 knee,39–43 hip,43–47 push,47–51 pull,51–55 brace;60s setup, groups60/120/180s. Each athlete has one set per role. Maximum bouts: squat25s, hinge21s, push17s, both-side bench row52s, heel-tap26s; supported breathing40s plus15s quiet recovery. The longest compact row ends232s and the final breathing recovery235s within240s. Equal blocks preserve push/pull teaching visibility despite different bilateral/per-side counts. Quiet time is feedback, recovery and setup, never bonus sets. P1 uses at least20s recovery before repeating its same basic marching/standing action: this is a four-step or two-second standing rehearsal at easy effort, so its preparation rest is explicitly shorter than the60s assigned to P2/E1 stationary practice. The earliest same-athlete P1→P2 stationary repetition has40s after P1 ends, exceeding20s. More recovery or an omitted later action remains appropriate if actual attention or control has declined.
alternatives:
**Long running not yet eligible:** keep one full35m corridor walk in E0 and use additional ordinary walking observations in E1: all ages D2standard/1compressed; L1standard/0compressed. Each long walking bout has45s active/orientation/exit and40s outside return, at least90s recovery. P2 is a15m ordinary walk with18s active+20s return. Comfortable walking/conduct and safe complete space remain necessary. No easy-jog or upright-running pass is recorded.

**Only the short corridor fits:** E0 is explicitly one full15m walk (20s active+20s return), not the35m walk. Eligible D E1 is standing-static5m low-intent start plus10m gradual runout, one attempt per set,2standard/1compressed,15s active+20s return and90s minimum recovery. P2 has the same short geometry at one counted easy rehearsal. This is contextual low-intent acceleration teaching using ACC-STATIC mechanics, not its85–100% output profile. Running initiation and safe runout need independent evidence. If those are unavailable, P2 uses18s short walking clearance and E1 uses20s short walking/orientation plus20s return, with the same mode-specific follow-up counts. All ages retain their actual setup; no start-type upgrade occurs. Record acceleration or walking, with upright-running space/permission unobserved.

**Travel unavailable but basic stationary rhythm eligible:** P2 and E1 use Basic alternating march in place: each set4individual steps,2each side×2s+2s settle, bodyweight, easy2/10 and60s recovery. P2 one set; E1 D2standard/1compressed, L1standard/0compressed for all ages. E0 uses one10s quiet-standing orientation while the coach explains the selected diagram; zero physical corridor travel. This is no-flight stationary practice, not exact traveling A-March, a run or a corridor pass.

**Marching also unavailable but quiet standing eligible:** replace the P1 basic march or any stationary P2/E1 bout with one10s no-step cycle per assigned set (2s settle,2s comfortable standing,6s reset), minimal effort. Minimum recovery is20s for P1 and60s for stationary P2/E1. E0 remains its one10s orientation. Both feet supported, arms relaxed, knees unlocked, no deliberate lowering. No appropriate safe task means defer that domain; symptoms or missing supervision are not solved by assigning more standing holds. Quiet-standing P1 can also be selected as a smaller rehearsal when marching ability is known. If P1 is standing because marching ability is unknown, later stationary marching still needs independent support-exchange evidence; standing supplies none.

**Supported breathing replaces heel taps:** all ages/all modes1×4comfortable breath cycles, nominal2s in/3s out without breath holds or forced depth. Calves and heels fully supported, both arms reaching, no heel pull or hip lift;20s total setup/exit makes40s, then15s quiet recovery. Five verified lower-leg supports are needed. Record supported breathing, not moving-limb competence.

**Already qualified suspension pull replaces bench row:** verified secure anchors, approximately70-degree body angle to floor, actual angle recorded. All ages D1×4bilateral reps, L1×3;2s lower/1s pull, at least5 good reps in reserve,5s handling and60s recovery. It replaces the single row set and requires its own support/grip/body-line participation; unsuitable bench fit does not establish suspension readiness.
workload_narrative:
The instructional base keeps its explicit no-flight actions and counted steps. P1 adds4basic march steps,2each side, or zero march steps on its standing route. P2 adds one5m low-intent start plus10m gradual runout, one15m walk, or its separately recorded stationary task. E0 always counts its selected whole-route observation:35m long walking,15m short walking, or zero travel; outside return distance/steps remain actual values rather than guessed totals.

On the long D running route, E1 adds40m standard or20m compressed easy running target distance, plus30m/15m gradual runoff. P2 adds its separate5m short target and10m runout; E0 adds35m walking. These are distinct tasks and intensities, not interchangeable sprint metres. Relative to OR-01’s short-start teaching, the longer target distance is an intentional new route demand with fewer recovered main running attempts and easy intent; no claim is made that the total distance is unchanged. OR-03 impact/stance fatigue can instead select the explicit walking/L route. Long walking follows its own35m outbound distances; short acceleration stays on its own5m target/10m runout record. Exact contacts, braking steps and all return metres remain unknown until observed. Zero intentional jumping does not mean zero running impact.

Strength plans five sets: one knee, one hip, one push, one both-side pull, one brace. D knee/hip/push is3reps for9–11 and4for12–14/15–18; L2/3/3. Squat tempo3s lower/1s pause/1s stand; hinge3s back/1s stand; push2s lower/1s press. Row D4each/L2each at4s per rep plus10s change/10s handling; heel-tap D2each/L1each at4s plus10s handling. Alternatives replace one set, not add one. Actual one-set history stays one; actual compatible two-set history is deliberately reduced. The familiar bilateral knee set resumes from its own actual record; it does not duplicate an additional split-stance set. Actual faults, omissions and modified routes replace any assumption that a full planned scenario occurred. No physical finisher or precise tumbling dose is invented.
final_tumbling:
Standard75–78 water/readiness,78–84 athlete/coach reflection on the finish/runoff/return and readiness for another attempt,84–88 record the next relevant module/main-entry choice,88–90 transfer. Compressed55–57 water/readiness,57–60 record/handoff. All ages add zero physical sets in this window.

The separate30min Body Control/Tumbling prescription remains UNRESOLVED: approved content, exact age/skill doses, mats and staffing are not supplied. Handoff actual walking/running/start distances, contacts/runoff, fatigue and coordination, all strength/support/grip/trunk work, and symptoms. Its coach independently verifies floor support and orientation prerequisites; no new complex inversion follows automatically. This handoff does not complete the separate program.
coach_record: Record actual prior exposures and current readiness; chosen base/P1/travel/support routes; verified corridor/start/finish/runoff/return and actual support/load; every attempt including faults and the counted E0 walk; actual walking/running/return distances, contacts, cue needs and response. Distinguish unobserved/needs_instruction/emerging/repeatable/modified/restricted by domain. OR-08 starts from the actual route and may change only a justified gradual intent; OR-12 later practices requesting/using recovery at retained conditions. No age, visit count or completed clock is a competency pass.
review_status: Independent programming critic PASS: counted corridor walk, distinct route/readiness identities, coach/return model, all-age prescriptions and retained strength. This does not verify actual delivery, current release or a complete separate tumbling prescription.

age_scaling_policy.equal_dose_reason: Short low-effort preparation is not age-based overload. Explicit equal doses across ages are deliberate; task skill, body size, comfortable range and current readiness decide the variant.
age_scaling_policy.readiness_independent_of_age: Experienced younger athletes may use qualified familiar actions; unfamiliar older athletes use instruction. Age never grants flight, rapid descent, floor support, loaded patterns or cue response.

layout_and_timing_assumptions.layout: Three columns of five distinct 3 m × 3 m personal bays: 15 independent working spaces. Five athletes share a lane assignment, never an overlapping crawl corridor.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.additional_space: Unobstructed peripheral coach circulation/access/egress and separately verified start, runoff and return corridors are additional to the 9 m × 15 m bay rectangle. The marked rectangle is not the total facility footprint.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.travel: Standing paths remain in personal bays. Short forward passes are at most 1.6 m; backward/lateral spans 1 m or less except 1.5 m carioca. Individually check full hand-walk/plank footprint before use.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.orientation: All bays face one end. Complete a pass and stop before ordinary walking return within that same bay. No crossing between athletes or concurrent opposite-direction traffic inside a bay.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.coaches: Familiar shared practice: one coach scans A/B and one scans B/C with clear oblique views. Three-wave teaching/checks: both coaches watch one active lane and split five athletes 2/3; other lanes stand. Clear views of all active feet/trunks are required.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.wave_handover: The active lane finishes standing, then the next lane starts on cue. The 2-second change (3 seconds for floor teaching) is a cue change, not relocation. Athletes stay in their own bays.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.equipment: Flat markers, bottles outside active rectangles, clean dry nonslip surface. No partner support, unstable props or unverified anchor is assumed.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.setup_before_clock: Mark/inspect space before class. Readiness/restriction information must be available. First demonstration includes stop cue and immediate comfort check. Unknown restrictions or inability to follow safe directions require individual resolution, never assumed clearance.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.clock_definition: Row time = demonstration + waves × individual execution envelope + explicit wave handovers + reset/transition. The individual envelope includes stated steps, pauses and returns. Shared practice means separate bays, not 15 times one athlete dose.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.tempo_rule: Execution envelopes are estimates for the stated variant, not speed commands. If safe learning/movement needs longer, use contingency, remove optional work or revise the booking. Never rush to validate arithmetic.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.bay_to_target_transition: Base ends at 12:00 full or 7:00 compact with athletes standing in bays. Reserve exactly 180 seconds for exactly two parent-owned target tasks. The parent exemplar defines the split and charges bay-to-start gathering, demonstrations, observed holds, rehearsal, exit and return within those 180 seconds. Use the parent-defined allocation; do not double-charge gathering or hide it before the base ends.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.physical_validation_status: UNVERIFIED: measured space, body fit, sightlines, surface, shared-floor schedule and target corridors have not been observed. Arithmetic does not certify physical feasibility.

teaching_and_competency_policy.full_familiar: Sixteen ordered slots with reminder demonstrations only. SP-11/SP-12 explicitly repeat mastered A-March because exact B/C identities are unverified.
teaching_and_competency_policy.compact_familiar: Eleven slots in original relative order. Omit SP-04, SP-10, SP-11, SP-12, SP-14. Retain floor purpose through the declared stationary-bear modification; hinge and squat remain last.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_full: Eleven recognizable slots in 12 minutes. Easy march replaces jog; optional crossing/flight/B/C complexity is omitted; lunges lose rotation/depth; floor flow becomes knees-down rock-backs; descent is slow; basic march/foot-roll precede observed hinge and partial squat-to-stand. After the easy raise, all actions are demonstrated and observed in three five-athlete waves.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_compact: Same eleven recognizable slots in 7 minutes. Basic walking/stepping/foot-roll can follow the coach in separate bays. Lunge, floor, slow drop, hinge and partial squat remain serialized in three observed five-athlete waves. One hinge and one squat cycle are readiness observations; qualification belongs to subsequent instructional work.
deferred_complexity: Traveling bear crawl and new complete plank/downward-dog flow
Full toe/ankle contact and overhead squat-to-stand range when unavailable
teaching_and_competency_policy.what_deferred_means: Practice the simpler named component in its original place; log performed variant and unfilled demand. Teach additional complexity in a relevant later instructional module. Do not silently pass it, substitute a generic unrelated warm-up or add teaching outside the clock.
teaching_and_competency_policy.partial_competency: Existing evidence can support a familiar variation, independently of age. Preparation completion does not unlock a main family: no-flight lowering is not landing, marching is not running, rock-back is not tumbling, and no throw/cue gate is tested here.
teaching_and_competency_policy.correction_limit: Use visible contingency for actual slower movement or brief corrective repeat and record time/dose/contacts. If essential teaching remains incomplete, mark profile/session REVISE and use the 12-minute instructional base or a justified booking adjustment. Never consume the reserved target time or speed up movement.
teaching_and_competency_policy.optional_reduction_order: For familiar full, remove SP-12 then SP-11, then SP-04/SP-10/SP-14 as readiness/purpose permits. Record omissions and revised clock. Compact/OR already omit these; beyond contingency, further necessary omissions require explicit review rather than an unqualified complete-base claim.

flight_not_qualified_overlay.application: For otherwise familiar athletes whose flight is unqualified, independent of age. This can accompany an independently qualified throw-only main branch, but does not itself authorize throwing or a cue.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-01: Easy march in place for the same 60 seconds full or 50 seconds compact; no flight.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-08: Retain a separately qualified no-flight rapid descent. If unlearned, slow drop squat to stick: 3 × 8-second envelopes, each 2 s lower + 2 s hold + 1 s stand + 3 s reset; no travel. Record changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-10: Omit four A-Skip hop landings; freed time is recovery, not another drill.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-13: Eight alternating no-flight foot-roll actions, four each side: 8 × 2 s + 4 s standing reset = 20 seconds; no travel. Log changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-14: Omit six bilateral pogo landing events; no substitute jump.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.accounting: Subtract omitted flight events and record actual time/contacts. Reduced-impact preparation grants no JUMP-T, REACT-T, throwing, early-release or go/no-go qualification.

records.name: Easy jog
records.purpose: Raise temperature and establish stop-on-cue and personal-space behavior.

card_mapping_status.limit: This in-place delivery preserves the jog purpose; exact bay-delivery mapping remains unverified.

records.setup: Center of the personal bay; no traveling loop. Bottle outside active rectangle. The demonstration includes a stop-cue rehearsal and immediate comfort check.
cues: Small relaxed steps; speak easily.
Freeze in your own space on cue.
stop_rules: Cease for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, loss of balance or inability to follow the stop cue; coach checks readiness.

competency_rule.observe: Relaxed rhythm, conversational breathing and independent stop without crossing the boundary.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Walking lunge with rotation/reach
records.purpose: Access comfortable split position, front-leg control and coordinated reach.

card_mapping_status.limit: A lunge matrix is related content, not approval for this precise forward-step/reach/return task.

records.setup: Forward step within a 1 m span, then return after each rep. Reach toward the front knee with a small comfortable trunk turn. First visit uses thigh contact and no rotation.
cues: Use a stable split base; lower only as far as controlled.
Turn gently toward the front leg and return tall.
common_errors: Forced depth or twisting over a painful knee.
stop_rules: Stop for pain or instability; use smaller split-stance bend if comfortable, otherwise omit and record.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable split position on both sides with stable foot pressure and smooth return.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Lateral lunge with reach
records.purpose: Access comfortable lateral hip shift and stable foot pressure.

verified_local_names: Lateral Lunge to Rotational Reach Flow
card_mapping_status.limit: The related flow includes rotation; this plain reach requires exact variant review.

records.setup: Step sideways within a 0.75 m span; shift into that hip, reach toward the thigh and return. First visit keeps hands on thigh and a shallow shift.
cues: Sit gently into the stepping hip.
Reach only with controlled trunk position.
common_errors: Chasing depth or lifting support foot unexpectedly.
stop_rules: Stop for unstable foot, discomfort or uncontrolled return.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable lateral shift and return both sides without forced depth.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog (ordered slot)
records.purpose: Prepare shoulder/wrist support, trunk control, hip movement and floor transitions with low fatigue.

verified_local_names: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog
Inchworm to World’s Greatest Stretch (related legacy flow)
card_mapping_status.limit: Exact composite not established. Stationary limb unloads explicitly replace traveling bear crawl for 15-bay delivery. Knees-down rock-backs are a declared partial-purpose regression, not an exact approved composite. The proposed stationary substitution is specifically four separately mastered single-limb lifts with full replants, not an unspecified weight shift or contralateral crawl.

records.setup: One athlete per dry nonslip 3 m × 3 m bay. Entire floor footprint fits before use. No shared slow-crawl lane or following crawler. Coach checks hand/knee comfort before support. Familiar bear support uses one limb at a time: left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot. A lift means the whole selected hand or foot briefly clears the floor by about 1–2 cm; it is not merely a weight shift. Fully replant and settle before the next limb.
cues: Hands comfortable; breathe with controlled trunk.
Quiet unhurried transitions; soft knees in downward dog.
Keep the trunk quiet; lift one contact only, then fully replant before the next.
Do not lift opposite hand and foot together.
common_errors: Forced straight knees or shoulder range.
Starting the next lift before the previous contact is fully replanted.
Rotating or sagging the trunk to clear the limb.
stop_rules: Stop for wrist/shoulder pain, slipping, trunk-control loss or inadequate footprint.
Use contingency or record incomplete rather than rushing floor entry.

Omit the familiar bear-lift component if any single-limb lift/replant has not already been mastered; use the entire named instructional floor profile and its coaching clock, or record incomplete purpose. No new bear-lift teaching is assumed inside the familiar reminder.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable actual support and floor entry/exit. Rock-back does not pass plank/bear or tumbling support. For familiar bear lifts, each selected contact clears briefly, fully replants, and the trunk remains quiet before the next lift.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

full.variant: Inchworm → high plank → stationary bear-position single-limb lifts/full replants → downward dog → standing

execution_segments.name: Move to hands-and-knees then low bear position
Left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot: one contact clears 1–2 cm then fully replants before the next
execution_segments.execution_detail: Per 2-second lift/replant: about 0.5 s clear the selected contact, 0.5 s fully replant, 1 s settle with all four contacts before the next lift; quiet trunk throughout.

full.tempo: Known controlled flow. Four single-limb lift/replant cycles at 2 s each: brief 0.5 s lift, 0.5 s full replant, 1 s stable reset. Do not start the next lift before stable full contact.
full.effort: Easy and conversational; no maximal speed, height, stretch or fatigue target.

rest.within_set: Only the pauses, resets and walking returns explicitly included in execution_segments.
rest.after_set: Use the row transition and next demonstration. Waiting waves add no repetitions. Extra required rest uses visible contingency, then an explicit reduction/revision.

full.other_contact_accounting: No intentional flight; ordinary support/steps are not scored plyometric landings.
full.prerequisite: Previously demonstrated comfortable floor access, wrist/shoulder support, brief plank, low bear position, EACH prescribed single-limb lift and full replant in left-hand/right-hand/left-foot/right-foot order with quiet trunk, downward-dog access and standing return. Plank/bear hold or weight-shift competence alone does not qualify the lifts. Verify body footprint fits.
full.contact_rule: One selected contact briefly off floor; other three remain planted. Full four-contact replant/reset before the next lift. No paired contralateral lift.
full.count_definition: One repetition requires completion of the entire ordered flow. Segment holds, transitions and four limb lift/full-replant actions are constituents, not additional flow repetitions.

count_reconciliation.calculation: One completed flow containing 4 individual lift/full-replant actions (left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot); do not sum heterogeneous segment counts into flow reps.
count_reconciliation.partial_cycle_rule: A fraction in conversion arithmetic is not an accepted partial repetition. Record completed whole cycles/actions/sequences actually performed.

contact_accounting.landing_event_unit: One landing event after flight; bilateral landing is one event involving two feet.
contact_accounting.foot_contact_unit: One foot contacting the surface; bilateral landing contributes two foot contacts.
contact_accounting.task_contact_scope: Where numeric, excludes ordinary walking returns; it does not mean all task contacts follow flight. Other ordinary step/support counts remain in the per-side/segment detail or actual log.
contact_accounting.unknown_count_rule: Null means not predetermined or not a total-contact prescription; never coerce it to zero. A zero flight count does not mean zero standing/support/step contacts.

compact.contact_rule: One selected contact briefly off floor; other three remain planted. Full four-contact replant/reset before the next lift. No paired contralateral lift.
compact.count_definition: One repetition requires completion of the entire ordered flow. Segment holds, transitions and four limb lift/full-replant actions are constituents, not additional flow repetitions.

count_reconciliation.calculation: One completed flow containing 4 individual lift/full-replant actions (left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot); do not sum heterogeneous segment counts into flow reps.
count_reconciliation.partial_cycle_rule: A fraction in conversion arithmetic is not an accepted partial repetition. Record completed whole cycles/actions/sequences actually performed.

contact_accounting.landing_event_unit: One landing event after flight; bilateral landing is one event involving two feet.
contact_accounting.foot_contact_unit: One foot contacting the surface; bilateral landing contributes two foot contacts.
contact_accounting.task_contact_scope: Where numeric, excludes ordinary walking returns; it does not mean all task contacts follow flight. Other ordinary step/support counts remain in the per-side/segment detail or actual log.
contact_accounting.unknown_count_rule: Null means not predetermined or not a total-contact prescription; never coerce it to zero. A zero flight count does not mean zero standing/support/step contacts.

records.setup: Same three five-athlete observation waves. Comfortable stance/reachable contact points; no forced toe touch or depth. Coaches see feet and trunk. Familiar source-linked sequence assigns LEFT reach and return, then RIGHT reach and return while the opposite hand maintains its comfortable toe/ankle contact; stand only after both reaches. Each reach stays in controlled comfortable range.
cues: Use comfortable range and a stable foot.
Reach without forced rib flare; stand smoothly.
Left reach and return, right reach and return, then stand; do not skip a side.
common_errors: Counting one reach as completion of the familiar sequential-bilateral cycle.
stop_rules: Stop for pain or uncontrolled balance/trunk; use declared partial sequence if comfortable. Longer teaching uses contingency or records incomplete.

count_reconciliation.partial_cycle_rule: A fraction in conversion arithmetic is not an accepted partial repetition. Record completed whole cycles/actions/sequences actually performed.

contact_accounting.landing_event_unit: One landing event after flight; bilateral landing is one event involving two feet.
contact_accounting.foot_contact_unit: One foot contacting the surface; bilateral landing contributes two foot contacts.
contact_accounting.task_contact_scope: Where numeric, excludes ordinary walking returns; it does not mean all task contacts follow flight. Other ordinary step/support counts remain in the per-side/segment detail or actual log.
contact_accounting.unknown_count_rule: Null means not predetermined or not a total-contact prescription; never coerce it to zero. A zero flight count does not mean zero standing/support/step contacts.

15-18.age_specific_delivery: Measure body-length/arm-span fit inside the bay; older age does not increase speed, travel, contacts or repetitions.

workload_and_tumbling_interface.purpose: Finish warm and organized, not tired. Effort about 2/10 and conversational; this is not overload or conditioning.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.full_flight: Four unilateral A-Skip hop landings and six bilateral pogo landing events are explicitly prescribed in the familiar full profile. Timed easy jog and ankling also carry impact; their actual flight/contact detail is recorded instead of fabricated.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.compact_flight: A-Skip/pogo are omitted, but easy jog still has impact and ankling actual contacts remain in the record. Compressed is not automatically impact-free.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.or01_flight: No intentional flight in the first-visit profiles; no landing gate is thereby passed.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.upper_body: Familiar floor work includes a 4-second high plank, brief bear-position support/unloads and downward-dog access. Count wrist/shoulder/trunk demand alongside throwing, pressing, bracing and separate tumbling. Rock-back support is still support.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.tumbling: The separate 30-minute tumbling/Body Control allocation remains unprescribed here. Share actual comfort, support/impact exposure and observations with its coach. Its later load and staffing remain unverified.

reviewable_modifications.change: Easy jog in place and shortened bay-contained travel replace starting-distance layout.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Keep purpose with no crossing or long queue travel.

reviewable_modifications.change: Stationary bear-position limb unloads replace traveling bear crawl in the familiar composite.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Five sequential slow crawlers per lane cannot be treated as simultaneous overlapping athletes.
reviewable_modifications.alternative_arithmetic: At 32 seconds per athlete, five serial waves in three parallel lanes require at least 160 seconds of work before demo/clearance, versus 32 seconds with separate bays: 128 seconds extra. Adding that to the complete full clock exceeds 720 seconds without another explicit change.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: Purpose-preserving proposal; exact composite and facility delivery remain unapproved.

reviewable_modifications.change: B/C ordered slots perform and record only mastered A-March; compact/OR omit them.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Do not invent an unverified B-march, hip-opening march or C-skip.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: B/C identity/delivery remains unresolved; short A-March profile also needs review.

reviewable_modifications.change: Familiar concluding squat-to-stand now uses four full or two compact complete 8-second LEFT-then-RIGHT reach cycles. Compact hinge remains two reps; OR01 compact remains one observed hinge and one partial squat cycle.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Preserve both source-assigned reaches, safe control and ordered three-wave observation within 720/420 seconds. This explicitly reduces the philosophy full starting dose of five to four; compact squat count changes from three ambiguous cycles to two complete cycles. The philosophy permits scaled repetitions.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: Coach-review adaptation of repetition count and delivery, not publication or operational approval. Brief readiness observations do not pass competence; finish required evidence in instructional work.

reviewable_modifications.change: First-visit flow, reach, descent and rhythm use explicitly simpler/no-flight components.
reviewable_modifications.reason: Teach recognizable components honestly instead of pretending reminder demos teach every complex action.
reviewable_modifications.review_status: If actual essential instruction exceeds contingency, mark REVISE and use longer instructional base or another justified booking change.

validation.count_accounting_status: PASS: all 192 age/profile dose objects have explicit primary count units; included numeric doses reconcile through segment primary-unit contributions; bilateral landings retain event/foot distinction; null unknown contact counts remain null; override routes resolve explicit dose/rest/profile references or explicit zero-dose omission.

counting_conventions.primary_repetitions: Always interpret reps_total with count_unit and count_definition. Mixed flow constituents, side counts, foot contacts and timed segments are not interchangeable.
counting_conventions.segment_repetitions: Each execution segment has its own count_unit. Its duration remains repetitions × seconds_each. Primary count contributions convert the segment counts to the record primary unit; complete cycles remain the accepted unit.
counting_conventions.SP-09_and_fallback_normalization: A-March primary counts are now individual steps: 8 familiar (4 each side) or 4 OR (2 each side). Bilateral cycle counts are explicit secondary metadata; actual movement/time unchanged.
counting_conventions.SP-13_correction: Familiar full/compact is 16 individual ankling task contacts, eight each foot; OR01 full/compact is four individual foot-roll/replace actions, two each foot. No execution duration or physical dose changed.
counting_conventions.contact_rule: Landing events and per-foot landing contacts are separate. Timed jogging/actual ankling flight count stays null when not predetermined, never zero by default.
